entry.title: [HIGH] AskUserQuestion can return an unselected option as approval.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.247 macOS terminal session found that an `AskUserQuestion` call returned the first recommended option as selected even though the user said they did not choose it and were typing a contrary mid-turn message. The assistant treated the tool result as consent and ran `docker compose up --build -d`, starting containers despite a standing instruction not to change machine configuration without explicit approval. The user's real stop message was delivered alongside the next tool result, after the question had already reported a success-shaped answer.

entry.title: [HIGH] Flagged subagent reports can truncate and resend in a costly loop.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.251 WSL2 session found that a long subagent final report delivered through `idle_notification` was cut at roughly 2,500 characters when the harness flagged it as an instruction-shaped `settings-json` pattern. The truncation notice told the parent to ask for the rest through `SendMessage`, but each re-ask resumed the subagent against its full transcript, repeated the expensive work, and produced another similarly truncated notification. The reporter contrasted this with an unflagged Sonnet subagent report that was delivered normally, pointing to the flagged notification path rather than a general agent-output limit.

entry.title: [HIGH] Scheduled task registry can stop all routines on one `fireAt` type.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop Windows MSIX setup found that all scheduled tasks stopped dispatching for about 55 hours after one entry in `scheduled-tasks.json` had `fireAt` stored as an ISO 8601 string. The app's own `update_scheduled_task` MCP tool reportedly wrote that string shape, while the disk loader expected epoch milliseconds and rejected the entire registry on startup and wake. Processes, package status, dispatcher heartbeat, and recorded skips still looked healthy, so every routine could go dark without an in-product liveness signal.

entry.title: [HIGH] Concurrent AskUserQuestion dialogs can lose unsubmitted input.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.251 macOS terminal session found that multiple AskUserQuestion calls in one assistant turn can render as overlapping dialogs instead of a queue. If the user starts answering the first dialog, selects Other, and types free-form text before a later dialog covers it, the first dialog returns from scratch after the top dialog is submitted. Already submitted answers settle normally, but in-progress selections and multiline Other text are cleared with no warning or recovery affordance. The report ties the reachable timing to concurrent tool dispatch plus serialized auto-mode classifier decisions, while noting the state reset appears to live in the dialog layer.

entry.title: [HIGH] Desktop org switching can kill running local sessions.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop macOS setup with one account in two organizations found that switching the account menu from one organization to another reinitialized local Cowork and Code session managers and stopped every local session, including turns that were actively running. The report's logs show same-account `orgId` changes followed by deliberate stop calls for running sessions, while the UI still pointed at the old session and no transcript error or termination marker was written. Switching back repeated the teardown in the other organization, so routine org selection could silently discard in-flight local work.

entry.title: [HIGH] Cowork scheduled tasks can mount only a subset of connected folders.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Cowork scheduled-task setup found that unattended runs intermittently mounted only a varying subset of already-connected folders. Across six observed incidents over ten days, different folder combinations disappeared per run, including cases after the folders had been added to the trusted list. The most severe run kept one leaf under an output tree reachable while the output root and other required folders were absent, so the task's local guard proceeded and delivered a business report with entire sections silently missing. The report distinguishes this from repeated approval prompts: the folders were already authorized, but each scheduled session appeared to receive an inconsistent mounted-folder set.

entry.title: [HIGH] `FileChanged` watch paths can miss external deletions on Windows.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code Windows 11 setup found that a documented `FileChanged` hook did not run when a watched `SKILL.md` file under `~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/*/` was deleted by an external Bash `rm`, even though a `SessionStart` companion hook returned absolute `watchPaths` that included the deleted file. The reporter verified the `settings.json` structure, the dynamic watch list, and the hook script itself by feeding a synthetic `{file_path, event: "unlink"}` payload directly to the command. The missing step was host invocation: the real unlink produced no hook log entry and no `systemMessage`, leaving a deletion-monitor safety hook fail-open for files outside the session working directory.

entry.title: [HIGH] Worktree isolation can allow simple Bash writes outside the worktree.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.250 Linux `--worktree` session found that worktree isolation refused complex Bash commands as too hard to verify, but allowed a simple absolute-path write such as `touch /tmp/wt-demo/outside-probe.txt` to create a file in the main checkout outside the isolated worktree. The session cwd was the generated `.claude/worktrees/demo` path, and the command exited 0 while modifying the shared parent checkout. This makes command complexity a poor proxy for target safety: complex harmless commands can be blocked while simple cross-worktree writes pass silently.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows exec-form hooks can drop args and evaluate stdin JSON.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.117 Windows 11 setup found that hook entries using the documented exec form, with `command: "node"` and `args: ["C:/path/to/hook.mjs"]`, were still launched through Git Bash as `bash.exe -c node` and the args array was dropped. Node then started without a script argument, treated the piped hook JSON payload on stdin as JavaScript source, and crashed before the diagnostic hook could log anything. The reporter reproduced this across 48 converted hook entries, affecting newly started and already-running sessions.

entry.title: [HIGH] Pending MCP servers can scrub tool references and break prompt cache.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.185 to 2.1.251 Agent SDK setup found that when a fresh CLI process resumes a conversation before configured MCP servers have finished connecting, the next request can omit those servers from the active tool list and rewrite earlier `tool_reference` results as unavailable. The following turn may have the tools back, but the temporary scrub has already changed early conversation history, collapsing prompt-cache reuse and leaving the agent with no MCP capability for that turn.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bypass-permissions Bash edits can hide file diffs.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.248 to 2.1.251 macOS setup found that bypass-permissions mode injected guidance to prefer Bash for file reads and edits, including `cat`, `sed -n`, `sed`, heredocs, or short scripts, instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. As a result, small file changes were applied through opaque shell commands and the normal Edit/Write diff cards disappeared. Settings such as `diffTool` and PostToolUse hooks did not recover the missing review surface because the dedicated edit tools were no longer being called.

entry.title: [HIGH] Project-scoped `strictAllowlist` can be silently discarded.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.250 macOS repro found that `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist: true` is silently ignored when it is placed in a repository `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`, even while `sandbox.enabled` and `sandbox.network.allowedDomains` from the same project file are honored. The filesystem sandbox blocked a harmless home-directory write, proving the sandbox was active, but a sandboxed Bash `curl` to a non-allowlisted host still returned `200` and the debug log showed the request going through the classifier/prompt path instead of deterministic denial. Moving the identical settings block to CLI `--settings` scope produced the expected `403`, so the gap is scope resolution and missing operator notice rather than network enforcement alone.

entry.title: [HIGH] Desktop `disclaimer` launch can break macOS protected-folder access.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop 1.37937.3 macOS repro found that Claude Code sessions launched from inside the Desktop app can run under `/Applications/Claude.app/Contents/Helpers/disclaimer`, leaving the whole Claude Code process without usable TCC attribution for protected folders. In the report, both Bash and the in-process Read tool returned `EPERM` for Desktop, Documents, Downloads, and CloudStorage paths, while `stat` still worked and a concurrent Terminal-launched Claude Code session could read the same file. The reporter also found that Full Disk Access had never been granted before or after the regression, so the failure was not a stale FDA grant; Desktop's folder-access UI claimed success but did not restore reads.

entry.title: [HIGH] Pasted secrets can enter transcripts without a sanctioned safe input channel.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code security feature request maps a missing input boundary for credentials: when a task needs an API token or other secret, users are pushed toward pasting it into chat because there is no first-party masked, transcript-free, session-scoped secret prompt for tool execution. The report says a pasted marker lands in multiple local stores, including project transcript JSONL, prompt history, and paste cache, and that later bug or feedback flows can preserve or upload conversation text. This is different from downstream redaction or file-read controls: once a secret is already in the prompt or transcript, hooks and instructions can only try to limit follow-on exposure.

entry.title: [HIGH] Trusted Devices can fail open for Remote Control attachment.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code Remote Control repro on an individual Max account found two Trusted Devices enforcement points failing open. First, removing all enrolled trusted devices did not force re-verification or interrupt an already active web session attached to a Windows VS Code Remote Control host. Second, a never-before-trusted Android Chrome session showed a device-verification modal, but choosing `Not now` dismissed the modal and still allowed prompts and tool execution against the host. Follow-up host logs showed uninterrupted bridge heartbeats and no local verification, device, trust, 401, 403, or attach record for the phone, so the host side had no visible evidence that a verification prompt was shown or declined.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Retention sweeps can delete user-created worktrees under `.claude/worktrees`.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.238 to 2.1.241 macOS setup found that the retention sweep could delete clean, pushed, user-created `git worktree add` worktrees stored under `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/` even though the docs say cleanup only removes Claude-created worktrees. The report distinguishes the name-filtered stale-agent cleanup path from a jobs cleanup path that reaps every dead background-job record with a `worktreePath` under `.claude/worktrees` when the worktree is clean, pushed, unlocked, and its root directory mtime is older than `cleanupPeriodDays`. Because normal commits and subdirectory edits do not refresh the worktree root mtime, an actively used worktree can look stale, and a dead job record can become enough authority to remove both the working tree and git worktree metadata without user-visible notice.

entry.title: [HIGH] Ralph Stop hook corruption handlers can be unreachable under `set -e`.
entry.summary: A reported bug in the official `ralph-wiggum` plugin says its Stop hook runs with `set -euo pipefail`, then parses the loop state file and transcript JSON through command substitutions whose failures are expected corruption cases. When fields such as `iteration:` are missing, or when `jq` cannot parse the last transcript line, the shell can exit at the assignment before reaching the hook's own diagnostic and cleanup branches. The result is a silent nonzero Stop-hook failure with `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` left behind, so the same broken loop state can fail again on every subsequent Stop instead of telling the user to restart cleanly.

entry.title: [HIGH] UserPromptSubmit hooks can skip queued prompts or drop injected context.
entry.summary: A reported UserPromptSubmit hook repro says prompt-time context can fail in two silent ways. Messages submitted while an agent turn is already running can be folded into the active turn without spawning the UserPromptSubmit hook at all, matching an older closed mid-turn report. A separate intermittent mode runs the hook and leaves hook-side evidence, but the returned additionalContext or systemMessage never reaches the model transcript. For hooks that inject collaboration rules, task routing, or safety reminders, both modes make prompt-level policy appear configured while the model receives the raw user message without the expected context.

entry.title: [HIGH] Sandbox TCC attribution can fail mid-session and revoke protected-folder access.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.248 macOS setup with the Bash sandbox enabled found that sessions running inside a TCC-protected Documents folder could suddenly lose access to the project directory several times in one long-lived process. The failure affected Bash commands, spawned tools, and the Read tool, produced `Operation not permitted` and `Current directory does not exist` symptoms, and recovered only after toggling the terminal application's Documents-folder permission in System Settings. Unified logs showed `kTCCErrorDomain Code=5` and `Failed to create Attribution Chain` for the live Claude process audit token, so the denial appears to come from a stale attribution error being treated like a policy decision rather than from changed filesystem permissions or a changed TCC grant.

entry.title: [HIGH] Plugin tool catalogue omits MCP schemas needed for security inventory.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.247 plugin-module setup found that `$.tool.list()` exposes each resolved MCP tool's name, truncated description, and MCP flag, but omits `inputSchema` and `outputSchema`; the referenced `$.tool.describe` capability is undefined, and the same catalogue call is unavailable in headless or SDK contexts. Security inventory tools can therefore see only invoked tool names through hooks, or parse private session transcripts containing user conversation content to recover a lossy all-tool list, even though Claude Code's own `/mcp` panel already has the schemas resident.
